Load count data from a creel connection

Source: R/fetch-loaders.R
fetch_counts.Rd

Reads the counts table from a creel data source, renames columns to canonical tidycreel names, coerces types, validates, and returns a data frame ready for tidycreel::add_counts().

The result carries up to three numeric count columns, so tidycreel::add_counts() cannot infer which one to expand into effort and will abort unless you name it. bank_anglers counts anglers on shore; angler_boats and non_ang_boats count boats, not anglers. Summing the three is therefore not a total angler count – converting boats to anglers needs a mean party size from the interviews, which is what tidycreel::derive_angler_count() applies:

counts <- fetch_counts(conn)
counts <- tidycreel::derive_angler_count(
  counts,
  bank       = bank_anglers,
  boat_count = angler_boats,
  party_size = mean_party_size   # from your interviews
)
design <- tidycreel::add_counts(design, counts, count_col = angler_count)

Naming count_col = bank_anglers instead is correct only on a fishery with no boat anglers; anywhere else it drops that component of effort silently.

Usage

fetch_counts(conn, ...)

Arguments

conn

A creel_connection object created by creel_connect().

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

A data frame with canonical columns: date (Date), bank_anglers (numeric), angler_boats (numeric), non_ang_boats (numeric), plus count_time (character) and any stratum columns the schema maps. Unmapped source columns are dropped.

On the API backend every row also carries creel_uid (character), the creel UID it was fetched for, so a connection to several creels returns them labelled rather than pooled.

When the API returns no rows, the result has no stratum columns. A fetch with rows carries each stratum in the source's own type, which an empty response does not reveal, and no zero-length guess binds with every type in dplyr::bind_rows(). Check for the column, or for nrow() == 0, before selecting a stratum.

The grain of a count row

One row is one count observation, not a day's total. Sources commonly record several counts on a sampled day, and it is the count time that tells them apart. Map count_time_col (CSV/SQL) or the count_time field (API field map) whenever the source records one, and pass the fetched column to tidycreel::add_counts():

design <- tidycreel::add_counts(
  design, counts,
  count_col      = angler_count,
  count_time_col = count_time
)

Without it, repeat rows on a date reach the design as separate sampled days: the day's effort is summed rather than averaged to a daily mean, and the within-day variance component is never computed (GH #129). fetch_counts() warns when it returns repeat rows and no count time was mapped.
